target.title: fix(discord): retry reply session init conflicts to prevent silent message loss
target.body:
Closes #102381

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord inbound messages could be silently dropped when a reply session initialization conflict (`reply session initialization conflicted for <sessionKey>`) raced with another turn finishing or another event initializing the same session. Telegram, Signal, and Slack already retry this transient condition; Discord did not, so the user saw no reply and the message was lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added bounded exponential backoff retry inside `processDiscordMessageInner` (`extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.ts`) to match the existing Telegram callback-submit pattern and Slack/Signal retry semantics. The retry only applies to the specific reply-session-init-conflict error string; all other errors fail fast on the first attempt. If the run is aborted while retrying, the loop stops cleanly and returns without throwing.

**ClawSweeper review follow-up:** the retry boundary was narrowed so context/history preparation runs exactly once and only the dispatch/session-init attempt is retried. This prevents a Discord room event from being recorded twice when a conflict happens.

## User Impact

Discord users are far less likely to see a missing reply after sending a message that races with a session teardown or concurrent turn. Operators no longer need to ask the user to re-send; the retry covers the brief window where the session store CAS conflict occurs.

## Evidence

- Added a focused regression test suite in `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts`:
  - retries with exponential backoff until dispatch succeeds (250 ms, 1000 ms, 2500 ms)
  - throws the last error after exhausting retries
  - does not retry unrelated dispatch errors
  - stops retrying when the abort signal fires
  - **records room event history exactly once across conflict retries** (new regression test for the narrowed boundary)
- Full local focused run:
  - `npx vitest run extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts` → 120 passed
  - `npx vitest run extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.queue.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts` → 22 passed
  - `npx vitest run extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.abort-skip.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.queue.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.preflight.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts` → 198 passed
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt` clean on changed files.

## Real behavior proof

This environment does not have the `crabbox` binary or a live Discord bot token, so a redacted live Discord conflict-to-success trace cannot be generated locally. Requesting maintainer help to run the Discord live transport / QA Lab proof on Crabbox, or a maintainer can trigger `@clawsweeper re-review` if the current in-process test evidence is sufficient.

target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators running `openclaw mcp login <name>` could see the OAuth login workflow hang indefinitely when the MCP server, OAuth discovery endpoint, or an upstream proxy stopped responding during the CLI login flow.

Before this patch, `mcp login` built an HTTP `fetchFn` via `buildMcpHttpFetch(...)` but did not pass the configured MCP `requestTimeoutMs` into the guarded fetch lifecycle. A stalled remote endpoint could leave the login command waiting forever with no deadline.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply the configured MCP `requestTimeoutMs` at the owning guarded HTTP fetch boundary: `mcp login` now passes `requestTimeoutMs: resolved.requestTimeoutMs` into `buildMcpHttpFetch`, which forwards it to `fetchWithSsrFGuard` as `timeoutMs` and keeps timeout refresh/cleanup tied to the managed response body stream. This replaces the earlier OAuth-only `wrapFetchWithTimeout` approach that cleared its timer as soon as response headers returned.

Scope stays CLI OAuth login only; broader MCP runtime/session transport timeouts are unchanged.

## User Impact

**Before:** `openclaw mcp login` could hang forever on a non-responding OAuth/discovery endpoint even when the MCP server had a configured timeout.

**After:** Configured MCP `requestTimeoutMs` values apply to CLI OAuth login HTTP requests through the guarded MCP fetch lifecycle; stalled endpoints abort with `TimeoutError` instead of blocking the operator indefinitely.

## Evidence

- `src/agents/mcp-http-fetch.ts` — optional `requestTimeoutMs` forwarded to guarded fetch `timeoutMs`
- `src/cli/mcp-cli.ts` — `mcp login` passes `requestTimeoutMs: resolved.requestTimeoutMs` into `buildMcpHttpFetch`
- Regression: `src/agents/mcp-http-fetch.test.ts` — hung-request timeout via guarded fetch
- Caller-path regression: `src/cli/mcp-cli.test.ts` — login wires `requestTimeoutMs: 9_000` into `buildMcpHttpFetch`

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** CLI MCP OAuth login no longer leaves OAuth HTTP requests unbounded when the remote endpoint stops responding before headers return; configured login timeouts abort with `TimeoutError` through the guarded MCP fetch lifecycle.
- **Canonical reachability path:** Operator runs `openclaw mcp login <name>` → `registerMcpCli` login handler → `resolveMcpTransportConfig` reads `requestTimeoutMs` → `buildMcpHttpFetch({ requestTimeoutMs })` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard({ timeoutMs })` → `runMcpOAuthLogin({ fetchFn })` → MCP SDK `auth(...)` OAuth HTTP fetch receives abort at deadline.
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime; production `buildMcpHttpFetch` + `mcp login` wiring exercised via colocated Vitest (no live stalled OAuth server in this environment).
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reuses existing guarded fetch timeout/refresh lifecycle in `fetchWithSsrFGuard` + `wrapGuardedBodyStream`; provider constraints N/A because this is CLI-local OAuth login HTTP wrapping.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, Node 22, source checkout on branch `codex/mcp-login-timeout`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/mcp-http-fetch.test.ts src/cli/mcp-cli.test.ts -t "aborts hung OAuth|configures enablement, timeouts, and OAuth login" --reporter=verbose
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text

 ✓ configures enablement, timeouts, and OAuth login 656ms
   buildMcpHttpFetch called with requestTimeoutMs: 9000

Test Files  3 passed (3)
     Tests  3 passed | 49 skipped (52)
```

- **Observed result after fix:** A hung OAuth fetch aborts at the configured deadline with `TimeoutError`; `mcp login` forwards the configured MCP timeout (`9_000` ms for `--timeout 9`) into `buildMcpHttpFetch`.
- **What was not tested:** Live `openclaw mcp login` against a real stalled OAuth/discovery endpoint; post-header body stall after partial chunk delivery (guarded fetch refresh is in place, but no dedicated stalled-body Vitest in this environment).

Related to #66561 (orthogonal — direct-invoke read benefits the embedded run-budget cascade but does not fix the underlying SSE timeout it describes; that issue should remain open). Narrow first landing of the broader direct-invoke umbrella tracked in #37131.

## Summary

Wire the `read` coding tool into the gateway direct-invoke surfaces (HTTP `POST /tools/invoke` AND SDK RPC `tools.invoke`, which share the resolver) so it is reachable for deterministic automation — CI/preflight checks, lint pipelines, browser capture flows — without an LLM round-trip.

**This PR is the redesigned narrow read-only landing.** Rebased onto current upstream `023ce6e96c38`. The exposure of `read` is now behind **triple-key gating** so neither the existing `gateway.tools.allow: ["read"]` knob nor the new opt-in silently grants host-FS read, and a non-owner trusted-proxy caller can never reach it.

## Triple-key gating (addresses ClawSweeper [P1] + owner hardening)

To reach `read` on the direct-invoke surface, ALL THREE must hold:

| Key | Purpose | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `gateway.tools.allow: ["read"]` | Lifts `read` from `DEFAULT_GATEWAY_HTTP_TOOL_DENY` (now extended with `"read"`). Existing knob; keeps the operator-acceptance step visible in the standard policy surface. | not present |
| `gateway.tools.directInvoke.hostFsRead: true` | **NEW.** Distinct surface-specific opt-in. Without this, `read` is not materialized into the candidate set even if `tools.allow` includes it. | `false` (omitted) |
| `senderIsOwner === true` | **NEW owner gate.** Host-filesystem read is materialized only for an owner/admin sender. A trusted-proxy `operator.write` caller is denied even with both config keys set. | n/a (per-request) |

**Any key alone (or any two) leaves `read` unreachable.** Old configs that already contain `allow: ["read"]` for unrelated reasons (e.g. an MCP/agent surface where `read` was always available) stay inert at the direct-invoke layer — no silent upgrade-time expansion — and even a fully-opted-in config refuses non-owner callers.

| `tools.allow` ⊇ `"read"` | `directInvoke.hostFsRead` | sender is owner | `read` reachable on direct-invoke |
|---|---|---|---|
| no  | no   | —   | ❌ |
| yes | no   | yes | ❌ (tool not materialized) |
| no  | yes  | yes | ❌ (filtered by HTTP deny) |
| yes | yes  | **no**  | ❌ (**owner gate**) |
| yes | yes  | yes | ✅ |

## Scope

- **Read-only.** Mutating coding primitives (`write` / `edit` / `apply_patch` / `exec` / `process`) are NOT exposed by this PR.
- **Both surfaces.** Gating applies to HTTP `POST /tools/invoke` AND the SDK-facing JSON-RPC `tools.invoke` (they share `resolveGatewayScopedTools`).
- **MCP loopback unaffected.** `surface === "loopback"` is not gated.
- **Hook-bypass safe.** Uses new `createOpenClawCodingToolsRaw` export (module-private Symbol marker, not reachable from typed SDK params) so HTTP-surface tools aren't double-wrapped — `handleToolsInvokeHttp` already runs `runBeforeToolCallHook` itself before dispatch.

## Files changed

- `src/agents/agent-tools.ts` — `SKIP_BEFORE_TOOL_CALL_HOOK` symbol + `createOpenClawCodingToolsRaw` export
- `src/config/types.gateway.ts` — `GatewayToolsConfig.directInvoke: GatewayDirectInvokeOptIns` field (new type)
- `src/security/dangerous-tools.ts` — `"read"` added to `DEFAULT_GATEWAY_HTTP_TOOL_DENY`
- `src/gateway/tool-resolution.ts` — triple-key gated materialization of `read` into the candidate set (`tools.allow` ∋ read AND `directInvoke.hostFsRead` AND `senderIsOwner`)
- `src/gateway/tools-invoke-http.test.ts` — real-transport owner/non-owner cases on HTTP `/tools/invoke` and RPC `tools.invoke`
- `src/security/audit-gateway-config.ts` — `gateway.tools_invoke_http.host_read_allow` finding (only fires when the config gates are set; silent otherwise since `read` is unreachable there)
- `src/security/audit-gateway-tools-http.test.ts` — test cases covering all gate combinations + vanilla
- `docs/gateway/tools-invoke-http-api.md` — operator-facing opt-in docs with config example + truth table
- `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` — `+1` surface-budget bump (4 dimensions) to admit the single new `GatewayDirectInvokeOptIns` public config type; no runtime impact

## Why a redesigned commit history (not a rebase of the prior 10)

The original PR's commits implemented an OLD design (single-key `allow: ["read"]` as the opt-in). The bot's P1 — "Require a fresh opt-in before enabling host reads" — needed a fundamentally different shape, not patches on top. Plus the prior commits referenced `src/agents/pi-tools.ts` which has been renamed to `src/agents/agent-tools.ts` upstream. The branch was reset onto upstream and the redesign written cleanly, then rebased again onto current upstream `023ce6e96c38`. Backup of pre-rebase history retained at `backup/read-only-pre-rebase-120fd2` on the public fork.

The final commit (`chore(plugin-sdk): bump surface budgets +1 for GatewayDirectInvokeOptIns`) is the only behavioural-neutral addition: the new public config type `GatewayDirectInvokeOptIns` adds exactly one top-level export, which the `plugin-sdk-surface-report --check` budget ratchet (run by `checks-node-core-fast`) counts against four dimensions (`config-types`, public exports, public function exports, public deprecated exports — the monolithic `config-types` entrypoint is `@deprecated`). target.body:
Closes #103538

## What Problem This Solves

Managed outgoing image preparation rejects a valid local `file://` URL even after resolving and authorizing its filesystem path. The unresolved URI text reaches `saveMediaSource`, which accepts local paths or HTTP(S) URLs and therefore tries to open the entire `file://...` string as a filename.

The failure is deterministic and still reproduces on current `main` at `a6bdc8092bf`. The equivalent absolute path already works.

## Why This Change Was Made

The managed-image owner now computes the local filesystem path once and carries that prepared fact through:

- display-name derivation;
- the existing local-root authorization check; and
- managed storage ingestion.

Remote HTTP(S) sources and image data URLs keep their existing paths. Local-root enforcement is unchanged. The returned display block contains only the managed URL and safe basename; the source path, query, and fragment do not escape.

This is the narrowest owner-boundary fix. Expanding `saveMediaSource` to accept another URL scheme would duplicate file-URL policy below the Gateway's existing resolver and risk inconsistent authorization. PR #103696 overlaps this repair, but this branch additionally includes focused path/file-URL parity and query/fragment privacy coverage plus the real storage proof below.

## User Impact

Callers of the Gateway managed outgoing image service can supply an allowed local image as either an absolute path or `file://` URL. The image is copied into managed outgoing storage and represented by a managed display URL instead of failing preparation.

No config, protocol, migration, dependency, or public Plugin SDK surface changes.

## Evidence

### Real managed-storage proof (no Vitest, no mocks)

Environment: macOS 26.5.1, Node 24.14.0. target.title: fix(cron): publish removals after durable commit
target.body:
Fixes #104078.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where external cron mirrors could observe a one-shot job as removed before OpenClaw had durably committed that deletion. If the final store write failed, the observer could cancel a wake for a job that still existed on disk, while the live Gateway could temporarily expose the speculative deletion.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Buffer automatic `removed` events for manual runs, normal timer runs, and startup catch-up until the final durable write succeeds.
- Restore the complete live cron topology, durable next-wake snapshot, and catch-up deferral ownership when that write fails.
- Keep the completed deleted-job snapshot for the eventual event, and remove an unreachable invalid-persisted-job deletion branch.
- Document `scheduled` and `removed` hook events as post-commit reconciliation hints.

The change preserves existing `started` and `finished` timing. It does not turn lifecycle hooks into an ordered delta stream; consumers should still reconcile the full durable cron view.

## User Impact

Plugin authors and host integrations can now treat `cron_changed` removal notifications as durable deletion facts. A failed cron-store write emits no removal, and subsequent cron reads continue to expose the still-durable job.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kx7fqgk4tjw6e9zw6dar21gs`: six new manual, timer, and startup-catch-up success/failure regressions passed.
- Same Testbox: 195 focused cron and Gateway hook tests passed across the new suite, one-shot behavior, startup catch-up, cron ops, timer regressions, and Gateway cron integration.
- Same Testbox: path-scoped `check:changed` passed, including core and test typechecks, lint, import-cycle, database-first storage, and runtime-sidecar guards.
- Source-blind live Gateway proof passed twice with distinct one-shot jobs: each emitted exactly `started` → `finished` → `removed`, the removed snapshot exactly matched the completed job snapshot, and loopback Admin `cron.list` already omitted the job inside the removal callback and afterward.
- Source-blind final-write fault injection was blocked: documented filesystem and SQLite locking surfaces could not safely isolate the deletion commit. The six focused tests provide the deterministic failed-write/no-removal/rollback proof.
- Docs MDX, i18n glossary, and formatting checks passed; targeted oxfmt and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh autoreview completed with no accepted/actionable findings (`patch is correct`, 0.93).

Release-note context: automatic cron removals now publish only after durable deletion succeeds and retain the full deleted-job snapshot.

AI-assisted implementation; maintainer-reviewed against current `main`. No agent transcript is included.

## What Problem This Solves

Closes #104077.

Cooperative suspension could report the Gateway ready while an ordinary plugin HTTP handler or plugin-owned WebSocket upgrade was still deciding ownership. New plugin work could also begin after the root-work fence closed, allowing a host to stop during untracked network or state side effects.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Move the canonical HTTP rejection and admission logic into a small Gateway boundary module shared by core and plugin routes.
- Acquire root admission only after plugin route matching and authentication, preserving exact/prefix fallthrough and avoiding false `503` responses for unmatched requests.
- Hold admission through each ordinary handler or upgrade ownership decision and release it on success, fallthrough, or error.
- Preserve the manifest-derived `gatewayMethodDispatch` entitlement for trusted control-plane HTTP routes. These routes may do bounded validation/discovery, but substantive work delegates through Gateway method dispatch so `gateway.suspend.prepare` remains a true root request.
- Keep established plugin WebSocket lifetime outside this patch; this change covers only the atomic upgrade ownership boundary.

## User Impact

Hosts can now rely on ordinary plugin HTTP handlers and new plugin WebSocket upgrades when evaluating suspension readiness. While prepared, those paths receive the same `503` boundary response as built-in HTTP work, while authenticated Admin HTTP suspension status and resume remain reachable.

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where file-transfer tar/dir-fetch stderr tail truncation can produce invalid Unicode when paths or archive listings contain emoji or other supplementary-plane characters.

`appendBoundedTextTail()` capped raw `child.stderr` chunks with `next.slice(-maxChars)` and failure reasons still used raw `stderr.slice(-200/-300)` at projection time. Tar stderr is unfiltered, so filenames like `📊report.csv` can land on a UTF-16 surrogate boundary and leave a lone high surrogate in error text surfaced to agents/operators.

**Concrete example:** `appendBoundedTextTail("prefix", Buffer.from("🤖tail"), 5)` with the old slice could keep `U+D83D` without its low half; `stderr.slice(-200)` on a ring buffer with emoji at the projection boundary had the same risk.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extract shared helpers in `extensions/file-transfer/src/shared/append-bounded-text-tail.ts`:

- `appendBoundedTextTail` — UTF-16-safe ring buffer for streaming stderr
- `projectBoundedTextTail` — UTF-16-safe final projection for error reasons

Both use `sliceUtf16Safe` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`, matching the SCP stderr fix (#103757) pattern. Ring-buffer sizes and tar/dir-fetch behavior are unchanged; only truncation boundaries are surrogate-safe end-to-end.

## User Impact

target.title: Fix stranded menu scroll after a manual refresh clears a provider error
target.body:
Fixes #2046.

## Problem

When a provider error (red multi-line banner in the top card) is present and the user clicks the persistent **Refresh** row, the refresh updates the open menu's cards in place — but a taller-than-screen tracked menu is left anchored mid-scroll: the viewport never returns to the top, and closing + reopening the menu is the only recovery.

## Fix (rev 3 — addresses both ClawSweeper findings)

Run a **viewport restore directly from the manual-refresh completion path**, bound to **the menu that initiated the refresh**: `refreshMenuProviderNow` captures the initiating menu's identity when the refresh starts, and completion restores only that same menu if it is still open, non-hosted, and dirty — one main-actor turn later so the unfrozen card layout settles.

- **Rev 2** (P1): the first revision armed a pending intent consumed only by an open-menu rebuild, but explicit store actions intentionally defer visible parent rebuilds while the menu is tracking — so the intent never fired on the reported flow and could linger for an unrelated later rebuild. The restore now executes from `startManualRefresh`'s completion with no pending state and no interaction with the rebuild path.
- **Rev 3** (P2): completion no longer scans all open dirty menus. Shared refresh invalidation dirties every open root menu, so a menu opened and scrolled while another menu's refresh was in flight could have been yanked to the top. The restore is keyed to the initiating menu ID captured at start; the menu-switch scenario has a dedicated regression test.

Background data ticks never take this path, so they can never move a viewport the user is reading.

## How the scroll repair works (probed on macOS 26.2)

Standalone AppKit probes against the view-based menu implementation (tall menu of custom-view rows, mutated and scrolled while tracking) established:

- A tracked menu is `NSPopupMenuWindow` → `NSMenuScrollView` (a real `NSScrollView`) → `NSClipView` → `NSTableViewBackedMenuRepresentation`, plus two arrow `NSImageView` strips.
- Row views are **recycled** once they scroll offscreen (`item.view` detaches; `enclosingScrollView` goes nil), so the shared scroll view is resolved through whichever item view is currently attached (`attachedMenuScrollView(in:)`).
- The offset is read and corrected with public API only: `NSView.enclosingScrollView`, `NSClipView.scroll(to:)`, `NSScrollView.reflectScrolledClipView(_:)`. The repair runs inside `performMenuMutationWithoutAnimation` and no-ops when the menu is not scrolled, not oversized, closed, or has no attached window.
- The flipped/non-flipped top-offset math is a pure helper (`menuViewportTopOffset`) with unit coverage.

## Verification

- `make test` — full suite green.
- `make check` — SwiftFormat + SwiftLint --strict clean.
- `swift test --filter StatusMenuViewportRestoreTests` — 9 tests.
- `swift test --filter StatusMenuOpenRefreshTests` — 31 tests green (the deferral baseline the review cited; this fix no longer interacts with the rebuild path at all).
- **End-to-end state test through the production path**: `manual refresh completion restores the open dirty menu viewport end to end` drives `performPersistentRefreshAction(in:)` (the same entry the persistent Refresh row and ⌘R use) on an open tracked menu and asserts the restore fires after completion **without any parent rebuild landing** (the test also asserts the menu is still dirty afterwards, i.e. the deferral behavior the review cited is preserved and the restore no longer depends on a rebuild).
- **Menu-switch regression test**: `menu opened during another menus in-flight refresh is never restored` starts a gated refresh from menu A, closes A, opens menu B mid-flight, completes the refresh, and asserts B is dirty from shared invalidation yet never restored. Companion negatives: a clean initiating menu is not restored; an initiating menu closed mid-flight gets no restore; background rebuilds never restore.

## Fresh-bundle proof status

I attempted the requested fresh-bundle recording and hit a data-safety wall I don't want to work around dishonestly: this machine is my daily driver with a live CodexBar install, and a debug bundle resolves the real user home for provider detection, local cost logs, and Codex auth — so even under an isolated `$HOME` the "synthetic" instance surfaces my real accounts and usage, and seeding `~/.codexbar/config.json` with synthetic providers would also reconfigure the live install. Producing the recording safely needs a clean macOS user account, which I'll set up if you want the video before merging.

Reproducible recipe (clean user account or sandbox machine): `./Scripts/package_app.sh debug` → launch → Debug pane → Error Simulation → set a multi-line error on Claude → make the menu taller than the screen (several providers or stacked token accounts) → open menu, scroll to the bottom, ⌘R → on this branch the viewport re-anchors at the top with the recovered header visible; on `main` it stays stranded.

No keychain access, no provider I/O, UI-layer only. CHANGELOG left untouched per house practice.

Suggested release-note line, if useful: *Menu: re-anchor the open menu at the top after a manual refresh, so a taller-than-screen menu is never stranded mid-scroll once a provider error banner clears; background refreshes never move the viewport.*

target.title: fix(cron): publish removals after durable commit
target.body:
Fixes #104078.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where external cron mirrors could observe a one-shot job as removed before OpenClaw had durably committed that deletion. If the final store write failed, the observer could cancel a wake for a job that still existed on disk, while the live Gateway could temporarily expose the speculative deletion.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Buffer automatic `removed` events for manual runs, normal timer runs, and startup catch-up until the final durable write succeeds.
- Restore the complete live cron topology, durable next-wake snapshot, and catch-up deferral ownership when that write fails.
- Keep the completed deleted-job snapshot for the eventual event, and remove an unreachable invalid-persisted-job deletion branch.
- Document `scheduled` and `removed` hook events as post-commit reconciliation hints.

The change preserves existing `started` and `finished` timing. It does not turn lifecycle hooks into an ordered delta stream; consumers should still reconcile the full durable cron view.

## User Impact

Plugin authors and host integrations can now treat `cron_changed` removal notifications as durable deletion facts. A failed cron-store write emits no removal, and subsequent cron reads continue to expose the still-durable job.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kx7fqgk4tjw6e9zw6dar21gs`: six new manual, timer, and startup-catch-up success/failure regressions passed.
- Same Testbox: 195 focused cron and Gateway hook tests passed across the new suite, one-shot behavior, startup catch-up, cron ops, timer regressions, and Gateway cron integration.
- Same Testbox: path-scoped `check:changed` passed, including core and test typechecks, lint, import-cycle, database-first storage, and runtime-sidecar guards.
- Source-blind live Gateway proof passed twice with distinct one-shot jobs: each emitted exactly `started` → `finished` → `removed`, the removed snapshot exactly matched the completed job snapshot, and loopback Admin `cron.list` already omitted the job inside the removal callback and afterward.
- Source-blind final-write fault injection was blocked: documented filesystem and SQLite locking surfaces could not safely isolate the deletion commit. The six focused tests provide the deterministic failed-write/no-removal/rollback proof.
- Docs MDX, i18n glossary, and formatting checks passed; targeted oxfmt and `git diff --check` passed.

target.title: fix(signal): surface daemon errors split across output chunks
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Signal operators running the auto-started `signal-cli` daemon could have an error line split across stdout or stderr chunks and forwarded as ordinary log fragments instead of one error diagnostic.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared Signal daemon output boundary now reads complete lines before applying the existing log classifier. This covers both stdout and stderr, preserves CRLF and LF input plus a final unterminated line, and does not change daemon lifecycle, configuration, or channel delivery behavior.

## User Impact

Signal daemon failures remain visible at the error level even when the operating system splits one log line across multiple stream chunks.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: real `signal-cli` daemon stderr split across child-process chunks is reconstructed before severity classification, so one daemon failure produces one error-level record.
- Current head: `9ea914269198d773adabe2a896ba16e4a78d3b06`.
- Real-daemon setup: OpenClaw's `spawnSignalDaemon` launched the official JVM release `signal-cli 0.14.5` in multi-account mode with an empty temporary data directory and no Signal account. The configured HTTP port was deliberately occupied so the real daemon emitted `Failed to initialize HTTP Server`. A byte-preserving relay limited stderr writes to at most 2 characters, forcing that diagnostic across child-process chunk boundaries.
- Redacted terminal transcript:

  ```text
  signal-cli version: signal-cli 0.14.5
  transport fault: stderr relayed in writes of at most 2 characters
  matching error-level records: 1
  signal-cli: Failed to initialize HTTP Server
  ```

- Focused regression: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/daemon.test.ts` passed all 5 tests.
- Targeted format: `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/signal/src/daemon.ts extensions/signal/src/daemon.test.ts` passed.
- Diff hygiene: `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD` passed.
- Autoreview: `python .agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` completed with no accepted/actionable findings.

target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Accidentally rejecting a skill proposal in the workshop currently has no undo path. The status machine is strictly one-way (`pending → rejected`), so a misclick forces users to recreate the entire proposal from scratch, losing all revision history and support files. target.body:
Closes #102064

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where scheduled agent work could lose its session state and final delivery when automatic session maintenance pruned or archived the session while the run was still active.

## Why This Change Was Made

Automatic maintenance now preserves every session identity covered by an active session-work admission, including aliases that resolve to the same session. Admission also crosses the session-store writer boundary and performs a final lifecycle revalidation, so maintenance cannot race between validation and active-work registration.

Explicit user-driven reset and deletion behavior is unchanged.

## User Impact

Long-running scheduled and gateway agent work can complete without automatic maintenance deleting its active session or causing an `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError`.

## Evidence

### Live scheduled-cron before/after proof

Run on July 11, 2026 using Blacksmith Testbox through Crabbox:

- Testbox: `tbx_01kx7py7cw0j3v5cgxyde14xgv` (`golden-crayfish`)
- Before fix: `9bfecf46ee3eb08173c97dd7d307363f67483edf`
- After fix: `c5a68cabe6aa45ec91a21279be42cfb64a374bd6`

1. Start a real OpenClaw Gateway with isolated state.
2. Add a scheduled isolated `agentTurn` cron job through the CLI.
3. Hold the turn at its second model request after `session_status` has run.
4. Force automatic maintenance by creating four additional sessions with `session.maintenance.maxEntries=2`.
5. Release the response and inspect cron terminal history.

target.title: fix: skip setup-only channel plugins in outbound resolution and drain pending deliveries on qqbot reconnect
target.body:
## Summary

When the qqbot WebSocket reconnects after a session timeout (close code `4009`), `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` returns a setup-only plugin stub that lacks any send capability. This causes the `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` error, and all messages queued during the disconnection window are permanently lost.

## Root Cause

`resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` resolves the first matching plugin entry for a channel id without verifying that the entry actually has send capability (`outbound.sendText`, `message.send.text`, etc.). During qqbot WebSocket reconnection, a setup-only plugin entry (registered for configuration/pairing but not for message delivery) shadows the real sending plugin, causing the resolution to short-circuit with a non-functional stub.

Regression introduced in 2026.5.28 (commit `e932160`).

## Fix

### 1. Split outbound channel resolution into shared and delivery paths (`channel-resolution.ts`)

Add a `channelPluginCanSend()` predicate that checks for any of the 10 known send methods across both the legacy `outbound` adapter and the newer `message.send` adapter:

- `outbound.sendText / sendMedia / sendPayload / sendPoll / sendFormattedText / sendFormattedMedia`
- `message.send.text / media / payload / poll`

Instead of gating the shared `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` resolver (which would break action-only channel plugins that have `actions.handleAction` but no send capability), a new **`resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`** resolver applies the send-capability guard exclusively for message delivery paths.

- **`resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`**: Shared resolver — returns any matching plugin regardless of send capability, preserving resolution for action dispatch, target resolution, and other non-send callers.
- **`resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`**: Delivery resolver — skips setup-only entries and only returns plugins that can actually send messages.
- **`resolveOutboundChannelMessageAdapter()`**: Updated to use the delivery resolver.
- **`message.ts`**: `sendMessage`/`sendPoll` updated to use the delivery resolver.

### 2. Align the direct delivery path with the operation-aware resolver (`deliver.ts`)

The preflight resolver was operation-aware, but the actual direct delivery handler reloaded the adapter capability-blind: `createChannelHandler` → `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` → `loadChannelOutboundAdapter` resolved the first registry entry for the channel id (`createChannelRegistryLoader((entry) => entry.plugin.outbound)`) without checking send capability. A setup-only shell with a defined-but-non-send `outbound` (`{ deliveryMode: "direct" }`, no `sendText`) pinned ahead of the runtime sender therefore still shadowed the real adapter on the direct send path, throwing `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` even after preflight had selected a valid plugin. This also affected the reconnect drain path, which has no preflight.

`loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` now resolves through the same `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()` resolver as preflight (with `allowBootstrap`, operation `text`), so preflight and the actual direct delivery handler share one send-capability-aware resolution path. The previous manual bootstrap-and-retry is removed because the resolver's `allowBootstrap` performs the equivalent lazy materialize-then-retry. The generic registry loader and the CLI/SDK surfaces are left untouched.

### 3. Drain pending deliveries on qqbot reconnect (`extensions/qqbot/src/channel.ts`)

The `onReady` and `onResumed` gateway callbacks now call `drainPendingDeliveries()` from the plugin SDK delivery queue runtime, recovering messages that were queued while the WebSocket was disconnected. The drain is:

- Filtered by channel (`qqbot`) and account id, with a fallback for default-account entries where `accountId` may be `undefined`
- Deduplicated via `drainKey` to prevent concurrent drains
- Wrapped in try/catch so drain failures do not break the reconnection flow

### 4. Route the gateway poll handler through the operation-aware resolver (`src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`)

The gateway `poll` handler still resolved its outbound plugin via the operation-blind `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`, while `sendPoll` (`message.ts`) and the direct text delivery path (`deliver.ts`) already routed through the operation-aware `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`. This left the gateway poll endpoint as the last surface where a setup-only / text-only first-match plugin could shadow a poll-capable runtime fallback and force a spurious `"unsupported poll channel"`, even though the new resolver test proves the poll-capable fallback should win.

The poll handler now resolves through `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery({ operation: "poll", allowBootstrap: true })`, mirroring the text delivery path. The `durationSeconds` / `isAnonymous` capability checks below the resolution now read from the same poll-capable plugin that serves `sendPoll`, so the capability gate and the actual send no longer disagree. The two non-poll resolver call sites in the same file (the `send` and `action` surfaces) are intentionally left on the shared resolver, since action-only plugins must still resolve without send capability.

## Tests

- `channel-resolution.test.ts`: setup-only plugin returns from shared resolver, action-only plugin resolves from shared but not delivery resolver, delivery resolver skips setup-only and returns sending fallback, legacy outbound adapter, poll-only outbound
- `deliver.test.ts`: new unmocked regression driving the real `deliverOutboundPayloads` → `createChannelHandler` → `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` path with a pinned setup-only shell that exposes a defined non-send `outbound` plus an active send-capable fallback, asserting the send-capable adapter actually delivers (fails before the Fix 2 alignment with `"Outbound not configured"`, passes after)
- `channel.test.ts`: onReady drain, onResumed drain

Fixes #88955.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: After a QQ Bot WebSocket disconnect (session takeover / close code 4009), `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` returned a setup-only plugin stub instead of the runtime entry, causing `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` and dropping all pending deliveries.

Zero occurrences of the `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` error across 18 reconnect cycles over a 4+ hour observation window.   **How the delivery queue works** (`deliver.ts:1254-1280`): Every outbound delivery is write-ahead enqueued via `enqueueDelivery()` before any send attempt. On success, `ackDelivery()` removes the entry (`deliver.ts:1367`). On throw, `failDelivery()` bumps `retryCount` and **leaves it pending** (`delivery-queue-storage.ts:137-144`).

  **What created the pending entries in #88955**: The `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` throw fired from `createChannelHandler` (`deliver.ts:223-231`) when `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery` returned a setup-only plugin with no send methods.   **Why transient QQ API failures also do not create pending entries**: The qqbot engine **swallows** HTTP/network errors into returned `{error}` result objects instead of throwing (`outbound.ts:301-304, 313-318`). A naturally-occurring live drain on the `onReady` path cannot be reliably reproduced because the fix removes the deterministic failure that created those entries, and startup recovery pre-empts the reconnect drain for entries present at boot. target.title: fix(shell): resolve pwsh.exe/.cmd/.bat on PATH for Windows shell discovery
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Windows, PowerShell 7 delivered via the Microsoft Store / App Execution Alias (and most portable installs) ships as `pwsh.exe`. `resolvePowerShellPath()` step 3 calls `resolveShellFromPath("pwsh")`, which only probed a **bare** `pwsh` with no extension. `fs.accessSync(entry/pwsh)` therefore returned `ENOENT`, so shell discovery fell through to Windows PowerShell 5.1 instead of using pwsh 7. This is the actual Windows pwsh resolution gap (distinct from the custom-shell `-c` args discussion in #104053).

## Evidence

Local reproduction on this Windows host (PowerShell 7.6.3 present only as the Store `pwsh.exe` alias, no `C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7`):
- `fs.accessSync("...\pwsh")` -> `ENOENT` (bare name missed by discovery)
- `fs.accessSync("...\pwsh.exe")` -> `OK` (extension probe hits it)
- After the fix, `resolveShellFromPath("pwsh")` returns the `pwsh.exe` path on PATH, and `resolvePowerShellPath()` prefers pwsh 7 over the 5.1 fallback.

This matches the source-level analysis: current main only looks for a bare `pwsh`, so a PATH entry containing only `pwsh.exe` is skipped before the Windows PowerShell 5.1 fallback (noted by the ClawSweeper review). The PR also adds Windows-only regression tests (guarded by `isWin` so Linux CI is unaffected): finds `pwsh.exe` when a bare `pwsh` is absent, prefers a bare `pwsh` match over `pwsh.exe` when both exist, and `resolvePowerShellPath()` resolves `pwsh.exe` on PATH instead of 5.1.

(Private paths and credentials redacted; this is a local OpenClaw gateway host.)

## Root cause

`resolveShellFromPath` joined the entry with the bare name and never tried executable extensions on Windows:

```ts
const candidate = path.join(entry, name); // only "pwsh", never "pwsh.exe"
```

## Fix

On `win32`, also probe `.exe`, mirroring the existing pattern already used by `resolveWindowsBashPath` (`"bash.exe"` / `"bash"`).

```ts
const executableExtensions = process.platform === "win32" ? [".exe"] : [];
const candidates = [base, ...executableExtensions.map((ext) => base + ext)];
```

**Scope note (addressed ClawSweeper review):** only `.exe` is added. `.cmd`/`.bat` are intentionally excluded because PTY execution (`createPtyAdapter`) spawns the resolved shell directly without child mode's `cmd.exe` wrapping, so a `pwsh.cmd` selected here could be chosen and then fail in PTY mode. `.exe` is directly executable in both child and PTY modes. Non-Windows behavior is unchanged.

This makes a Store/portable `pwsh.exe` discoverable on PATH, so `resolvePowerShellPath()` prefers pwsh 7 over 5.1.

## Test plan

Windows-only tests in `shell-utils.test.ts` (guarded by `isWin` so Linux CI is unaffected):
- finds `pwsh.exe` when a bare `pwsh` is absent
- prefers a bare `pwsh` match over `pwsh.exe` when both exist
- `resolvePowerShellPath()` resolves `pwsh.exe` on PATH instead of 5.1 when standard install dirs are empty

Existing tests unchanged; non-Windows `resolveShellFromPath` behavior preserved.

target.title: fix(agents): add size limit to LSP message parser
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: The LSP message parser accepted unbounded `Content-Length`
values. A malicious or misbehaving LSP server could send an arbitrarily
large `Content-Length` header, causing unbounded buffer allocation and
memory exhaustion. Additionally, a very long decimal `Content-Length`
(e.g., 400+ digits) causes `Number.parseInt` to return `Infinity`, which
was stored as an infinite drain counter — permanently suppressing all
future LSP output and leaving pending requests to time out.

**Root cause**: When `Content-Length` exceeded the 10 MB limit, the parser
only skipped the header + separator bytes but kept the declared body in
`session.buffer`. If the oversized body arrived across multiple stream
chunks, the buffer would grow unboundedly. For non-safe integer lengths
(`Infinity` from `parseInt`), the arithmetic computed `bodyStart + Infinity
= Infinity`, storing an infinite `oversizeDrainRemaining` that never
decrements. Additionally, when the final drain chunk exactly matched the
remaining byte count, the handler returned early without failing the
session, leaving the pending request to time out.

**Solution**: Add a 10 MB `Content-Length` limit that fully drains the
declared oversized body when the frame is completely buffered, or tracks
remaining bytes to skip via `session.oversizeDrainRemaining` when the body
arrives across chunks. Non-safe integer Content-Length values (Infinity)
are detected before drain arithmetic and signal a fatal protocol error.
Finite oversized frames (>10 MB but still a safe integer) trigger session
failure after dispatching any valid responses parsed before the oversized
frame — the associated pending request is rejected immediately instead of
waiting for the normal request timeout. The exact-match drain completion
boundary (`raw.length === oversizeDrainRemaining`) now falls through to
the session failure check instead of returning early.

**What changed**: `src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.ts`
- `parseLspMessages`: accepts optional `oversizeDrainRemaining` out-param
  with `fatal` flag; on oversized frames drains the full frame or signals
  remaining bytes and sets the fatal flag. On non-safe integer
  Content-Length signals a fatal condition via NaN.
- `handleIncomingData`: drains `session.oversizeDrainRemaining` from raw
  stream data before appending to the parse buffer. Detects non-finite
  drain remaining or drained finite oversized frames and calls
  `failLspSession` after dispatching any completed responses parsed
  before the bad header. Fixed the exact-match drain boundary: changed
  `<=` to `<` so the exact-match case continues into session failure.
- `LspSession` type: added `oversizeDrainRemaining: number`,
  `oversizeDrainSeen: boolean`

**What did NOT change**: Valid message parsing, session lifecycle, tool
materialization — all unchanged for frames within the 10 MB limit.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: LSP message parser now closes three gaps:
1) fully drains finite oversized Content-Length frames (>10 MB) to
prevent memory exhaustion, 2) fails the session for non-safe integer
Content-Length (Infinity from parseInt) instead of permanently suppressing
all future LSP output, and 3) fails the session for finite oversized
frames after dispatching any valid responses parsed before the oversized
frame so the associated pending request is rejected immediately instead
of timing out.

**Real environment tested**: Linux 4.19.112, Node 22.19.0, pnpm 11.2.2

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
pnpm test src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All 18 tests pass, including 4 new
handler-level tests for finite oversized Content-Length session failure.

**Before-fix behavior (if applicable)**: Finite oversized frames (>10 MB)
were silently drained without failing the session, leaving the associated
pending request to time out after 10 seconds instead of failing
immediately. When the final drain chunk exactly matched the remaining
oversized body bytes, the handler returned early with a zero counter
without failing the session.

**After-fix evidence**:

All 18 tests pass:
```text
 ✓ bundle LSP runtime > oversized Content-Length handling (2)
 ✓ bundle LSP runtime > unsafe Content-Length handling (4)
 ✓ bundle LSP runtime > finite oversized Content-Length handling (4)
   ✓ sets fatal flag on parseLspMessages oversizeDrain
```

target.title: fix(tools-manager): bound GitHub releases response body to prevent unbounded read
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The agent helper-tool fallback for `fd` and `ripgrep` read GitHub's latest-release response with `Response.json()`. That consumes the complete remote body before parsing it, so a faulty or compromised response could grow agent memory without a bound.

The affected path is `ensureTool`, reached by the agent `find` and `grep` tools when no suitable local binary is available. The unbounded behavior shipped in `v2026.5.28`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The maintainer candidate reads the response through the shared `@openclaw/media-core/read-response-with-limit` helper with an owner-local 1 MiB cap. The two current GitHub responses are about 37 KiB and 51 KiB, leaving more than 20x headroom without importing the provider setup helper's unrelated 16 MiB policy.

The implementation also:

- distinguishes overflow, malformed JSON, missing/invalid `tag_name`, abort, release-status, and download-status failures;
- cancels oversized bodies and always releases the guarded response in `finally`;
- propagates failures from silent automatic resolution so `find`/`grep` report the actionable cause instead of masking corruption as a generic missing tool;
- preserves non-silent log-and-return behavior and existing system/local fallback behavior.

A `Content-Length` check alone would not protect chunked responses, and changing the shared helper or a global cap would broaden the owner boundary unnecessarily.

## User Impact

target.title: fix(agents): lease session worktrees during runs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where a resumed session's agent run could lose its managed worktree checkout mid-run: idle GC or a separate remover could delete the session's isolated checkout while the run was using it, destroying in-flight workspace files. It also fixes the silent counterpart, where a session whose managed worktree had already been removed was admitted anyway and ran without its checkout as if it were an ordinary directory.

## Why This Change Was Made

The managed-worktree service now owns a per-worktree FIFO lease, and agent command preparation acquires it as soon as the session cwd resolves, before any workspace-dependent step, releasing it in the run's outer cleanup. The lease retains the existing PID-tagged Git worktree lock with local reference counting, so both same-process removal paths and separate-service removers are excluded while a run is active. Admission for a cwd that belongs to a removed managed worktree now fails with `managed worktree was removed: <path>` instead of proceeding. Explicit removal keeps its existing force semantics.

## User Impact

Users resuming sessions with isolated worktrees can no longer have their live checkout deleted underneath an active run by idle GC or session cleanup, including when the session works in a subdirectory of the worktree. A session whose checkout was removed while it was away now fails fast with a clear error instead of silently continuing without its files.

## Evidence

- Rebased onto current `origin/main` (67e1d43911), resolving the `WorktreeSnapshotError` conflict in `src/agents/worktrees/service.ts` in favor of the typed error from main.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/worktrees/service.test.ts src/agents/command/worktree-lease.test.ts`: 32 passed, including a new removed-path admission regression.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agent.worktree-race.test.ts`: 2 passed; the composed regression pauses real preparation while removal races, covering both the run-wins ordering and the removal-wins-before-admission ordering.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agent.test.ts`: 35 passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agent.acp.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.delete-lifecycle.test.ts`: 102 passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` and `oxfmt --check` on all changed files: clean.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` and `-p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json`: clean.

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: a resumed session's agent run must keep its managed worktree checkout while cleanup or a separate remover races it, and a session whose managed worktree was already removed must fail admission instead of silently running in a recreated ordinary directory.
Real environment tested: the production agent command preparation path and ManagedWorktreeService driven end to end on a clean AWS machine (Crabbox lease cbx_619103fb2076, c7a.xlarge), with real on-disk git repositories, real managed worktree creation, and real registry state, comparing pristine main 67e1d43911 against this patch f12f79032a on identical inputs.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `crabbox run --provider aws --id cbx_619103fb2076 --shell -- "bash run.sh"`, where the script creates a session-owned worktree with a nested workspace directory, seeds the session with that cwd, admits the run through the production preparation entry point, races a separate service's non-force removal, releases the run, then removes a second worktree and attempts admission for it again.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 67e1d43911)
# scenario 1: separate remover races an admitted session run
session admitted with nested managed cwd: true
separate non-force removal reports the live worktree lock: false
nested session directory exists after the removal attempt: false
run admission holds a releasable worktree lease: false
removal after the session run ends: error: unknown active worktree: b4242765-4c49-4ddc-934d-69698e802427
# scenario 2: removal wins before session admission
managed checkout removed before admission: true
session preparation proceeded without its managed worktree: true
preparation still points at the removed cwd: true
# AFTER (this patch f12f79032a, identical inputs)
# scenario 1: separate remover races an admitted session run
session admitted with nested managed cwd: true
separate non-force removal reports the live worktree lock: true
nested session directory exists after the removal attempt: true
run admission holds a releasable worktree lease: true
removal after the session run ends: removed
# scenario 2: removal wins before session admission
managed checkout removed before admission: true
session preparation fails with: managed worktree was removed: /tmp/openclaw-proof-bvGt15/.openclaw/worktrees/861311bf01e8bf89/proof-removed
managed checkout recreated as ordinary directory: false
```
Observed result after fix: an admitted run holds a releasable lease backed by the live worktree lock, a separate non-force remover is rejected while the run is active and succeeds after the run ends, and admission for a removed managed path fails with a clear error instead of proceeding without its checkout.
What was not tested: no live provider request or multi-process gateway deployment was exercised; the two racing services ran in one process on the remote machine, with cross-process protection relying on the directly verified on-disk Git worktree lock.

## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
